newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's Mugabe says no to S.African request.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Mugabe says no to S.African request.

text.p: Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe has rejected a request by South Africa to release five Zimbabweans jailed for offences linked to an apartheid-era sabotage campaign, the Financial Gazette reported on Thursday.

Mugabe told the privately owned paper in an interview he had made it clear to his South African counterpart Nelson Mandela during a state visit last week that the prisoners would remain in Zimbabwean custody.
"We will keep these people in prison until such time that we are satisfied we should release them, if at all we will release them," Mugabe said.

Kevin Woods, Philip Conjwayo, Michael Smith and Barry Bawden were jailed for life in 1988 for a spate of bombings at several African National Congress homes in Zimbabwe when South Africa's now-ruling party was still outlawed.
Another man, Dennis Beaham, was sentenced to 20 years for trying to help them escape prison.

Mugabe dismissed an assertion by Mandela's government that the five, granted South African citizenship by the Pretoria government soon after their arrests, should be freed in line with a general amnesty the ANC proclaimed when it assumed power in 1994.
"I don't know how they can become South African citizens because I don't know whether the South African citizenship can be bestowed by remote control," Mugabe said.

"President Mandela did not raise the issue of citizenship with me. These are Zimbabweans who violated Zimbabwean laws and people who violate our laws are subject to punishment within the framework of our laws here."
The families of the five have held protests in South Africa and petitioned the government to help secure their return, saying they had failed to gain access to the Zimbabwean president.
